text:
Sam Park: quick brain dump — trying a cheap spec-decode probe on the new 13B-quant build, curious about eval protocol ideas.
Jia Li: nice, key q: are we measuring token-level accuracy vs. baseline or end-task pass rates?
Sam Park: start simple: perplexity + exact-match on our smol QA suite, but we need latency token/time and token-cost too.
Matt O'Connor: +1. also watch for rare token drift after quant. saw hallucination spikes before.
Jia Li: for speculative decode we should record: (1) speculative acceptance rate, (2) fallback rate, (3) latency delta p50/p95, (4) token overhead.
Sam Park: agreed. rough plan: run 10k prompts from onboard bench, run baseline greedy on float model, run quant+spec with two abort thresholds (0.6, 0.8) and beam-size 1.
Matt O'Connor: can you paste the run config? want to reproduce on my dev pool.
Sam Park: sure — local snippet:
```
MODEL=redwood-13b-quant-v2
SPECD=on
THRESHOLDS=(0.6 0.8)
TIMEOUT_MS=1000
BATCH=8
EVAL_SET=onboard_qa_10k.jsonl
```
Jia Li: also log the first-token-time and kv-cache hit/miss counts. speculative can hide upstream cost if we don't track cache priming.
Sam Park: good call. will capture `first_token_ms`, `total_tokens_sent_to_model`, `fallback_count`, `spec_accept_count`.
ops-bot: deploy-notice: spec-decode-job queued on dev-dedicated-02 (ETA ~ 15m) :gear:
Matt O'Connor: do one small manual eyeball run on 200 prompts and paste a few failure cases here. I'd like examples of where spec accepted a wrong token faster.
Sam Park: will do. initial hypothesis: spec increases p50 by ~10-20ms but reduces p95 by offloading tail? might be the opposite depending on threshold.
Jia Li: evaluation metric idea: weighted utility = 0.7 * task_score + 0.2 * normalized_latency + 0.1 * tokens_overhead_penalty. gives single-number tradeoff to compare across thresholds.
Matt O'Connor: fine, but keep raw metrics too. aggregated metrics can hide mode failures.
Sam Park: agreed. i'll attach both CSV and per-prompt diffs. plan to run full 10k overnight. posting quick 200-run summary in ~30m.
Jia Li: one more: add the quantization debug flag to emit per-layer activation drift for first 128 tokens so we can see where topk probs diverge.
Sam Park: ok -- adding `--debug-activation-deltas=128`.
Matt O'Connor: if we see degenerate loops/echo, include nll traces and sample seeds.
Sam Park: noted. thanks team. will post raw logs + a tiny set of worst regressions.
Jia Li: :thumbsup: excited to see tradeoffs.
Matt O'Connor: +1. ping me in thread when results land.
Sam Park: will do.
